lesson.title: Weil der Bus zu spät war

sentences.text: Mina kommt zu spät zu einem Termin im Büro.
sentences.natural_meaning: Mina arrives late for an appointment at the office.

verb_help.usage: The sentence uses the present tense for a current action, routine, plan, or general fact.

sentences.text: Ihr Chef fragt freundlich: „Warum bist du heute zu spät?“
sentences.natural_meaning: Her manager asks politely, “Why are you late today?”

verb_help.usage: The sentence uses the present tense for a current action, routine, plan, or general fact.

items.german: Warum bist du heute zu spät

sentences.text: Mina antwortet: „Ich bin zu spät, weil der Bus eine Verspätung hatte.“
sentences.natural_meaning: Mina replies, “I am late because the bus was delayed.”

verb_help.usage: The sentence uses the present tense for a current action, routine, plan, or general fact.

This is a simple-past form. In speech it is especially common with sein, haben, and modal verbs.

items.german: weil der Bus eine Verspätung hatte

sentences.text: Sie hat zwanzig Minuten gewartet und im Bus sofort angerufen.
sentences.natural_meaning: She waited for twenty minutes and called immediately from the bus.

verb_help.usage: The sentence uses the present tense for a current action, routine, plan, or general fact.
gewartet is the past participle of warten; it combines with haben to form the conversational past.
angerufen is the past participle of anrufen; it combines with haben to form the conversational past.

sentences.text: Der Chef sagt: „Danke für den Bescheid; jetzt ist der Grund klar.“
sentences.natural_meaning: The manager says, “Thanks for letting me know; now the reason is clear.”
